CIVIC CURRICULUM / WORK SAMPLE

Other work

Work for other audiences: a self-paced course, client work, an interactive tool and K-12 lessons.

Different topics, same skill: learn a new subject and audience quickly, then turn it into something people can use.

INSIDE THIS SAMPLEDesign rationaleSelf-paced course design: Grants Administration EssentialsClient work, tools and lessons

Design rationale

The learner
Reviewers want to see range without losing sight of the role. Each piece below says what carries over to city-practitioner learning.
The approach
Group by format rather than by topic; keep each item short and labeled with role, year and audience.
The intended outcome
Supporting evidence of range. The civic work samples remain the core of this portfolio.

Self-paced course design: Grants Administration Essentials

(Year, client and candidate role: confirm with candidate) · Audience: university grants staff new to the work

Relevant to this role: the same structure could turn a live WWC session into a self-paced pathway with practice, checks and an on-the-job application task.

Client work, tools and lessons

CLIENT WORK · RANDOM HOUSE · (year)

Step into Reading 25th Anniversary: learn to read & make your own story

An interactive game for Random House’s Step into Reading 25th anniversary campaign. It took young readers from reading a story to building one of their own. (Candidate role, scope and outcome: confirm with candidate)

Relevant to this role: scaffolded, game-style learning that builds a skill step by step until learners can create something themselves, delivered for a major brand client.

CLIENT WORK · RESEARCH COMMUNICATION · (year)

Research findings website

A website built for a researcher to present and explore their findings. (Researcher or field, audience, candidate role and link: confirm with candidate)

Relevant to this role: translating research into a clear, usable format for a non-specialist audience. This is the core task of turning research into practical curriculum.

INTERACTIVE TOOL · PROTOTYPE · (year)

Which UX method should I use? An interactive method picker

Answer a few questions about where a project stands and the tool recommends three methods from a 153-card library, explains why each fits and what to do next.

Relevant to this role: turning a large technical resource library into a decision aid. WWC could use the same pattern to help staff choose an evidence practice or tool.

Open the prototype

STEM OUTREACH · K-12 · (year)

Waves that carry information: a 2nd/7th/11th-grade lesson suite

Three 45-minute, substitute-ready lessons on one science idea, aligned vertically across grade levels to NM STEM Ready!/NGSS standards using the 5E model.

Relevant to this role: adapting one body of technical content for three very different audiences and levels of experience, plus materials someone else can deliver.
